gloss: to be proud, to hold one's head high

definitions.gloss: to be proud, to hold one's head high with confidence
definitions.explanation: To feel and display pride or confidence, often shown through upright posture.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}れる→張る：12583_haru⟧。
examples.english: I can be proud of my work.

examples.japanese: ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}って→張る：12583_haru⟧⟦{生|い}きていきたい→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧。
examples.english: I want to live with my head held high.

examples.japanese: ⟦{堂々|どうどう}→堂々：05895_doudou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}って→張る：12583_haru⟧⟦{歩|ある}いた→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: She walked confidently with her chest out.
It's something I can say proudly.

examples.english: I want to be an adult who can hold my head high in front of children. I want to live honestly.

notes:
STRUCTURE: ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧ (chest) + ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ + ⟦{張|は}る→張る：12583_haru⟧ (to stretch, to draw taut) — the posture of pride, chest out and shoulders back.

NUANCE: Pride that is earned, not arrogance. It is used for pride in work well done, for living without anything to hide, and for standing behind one's choices. Because the pride has to be justified, the phrase often appears as a test the speaker sets for themself: can I say this ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}って→張る：12583_haru⟧?

POTENTIAL FORM: ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}れる→張る：12583_haru⟧ ('can hold one's head high') is at least as common as the plain form, and is the usual shape when talking about oneself:
- ⟦{胸|むね}→胸：00972_mune⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{張|は}って→張る：12583_haru⟧⟦{言|い}える→言う：00515_iu⟧: can say it proudly
